newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders steady.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to off, feeders steady.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent lower while feeder cattle were called steady, livestock analysts said.
Slow fed cattle trade and an uneven boxed beef market were expected to provide further pressure to live cattle futures early. Lack of feedlot trade has put futures on the defensive, analysts said.

However, expectations continued that packers will pay up soon for cattle. Beef promotions should expand after the holiday and packers will need to obtain some cattle soon to meet slaughter needs into early next week, they said.
Action in pork pits with the developments in Taiwan and in anticipation of the upcoming hogs and pigs report will also influence live cattle futures, they said.
Feeder cattle were expected to show little price movement as the index was virtually unchanged and corn futures were called steady, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.03 at $69.35 per cwt.
